long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Ryland went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: Ryland provided all of the offense for Arizona in Week 10, making multiple field goals in a contest for the fourth time in the last five weeks. The kicker has rebounded well in 2026 after a challenging 2025 campaign, converting 22 of 24 field-goal tries over 10 contests so far this season.

short_comment: Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.
long_comment: With Bam Knight back in the lineup in Week 10 after one absence due to a concussion, Allgeier didn't reach double-digit touches for the first time since Week 5, a span in which the latter's 65 touches went for 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Knight himself found a similar lack of success Sunday with just 19 yards on his five rushes. Because the Cardinals racked up just 123 yards of offense in rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start, it's tough to envision worse outcomes moving forward, though the team does take on the surging Chiefs next Sunday on the road.

short_comment: McBride tallied five catches on as many targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
long_comment: McBride's streak of at least seven catches ended at 11 games, and his receiving yardage total marked his second-fewest of the campaign in what doubled as rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start. Better days likely are ahead for the duo, but as McBride works with his third signal-caller this season -- and the least experienced one at that after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew -- there may be more lows than highs for the tight end over the final seven contests. McBride will look to bounce back next Sunday at Kansas City.

short_comment: Hellams logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
long_comment: Hellams racked up tackles in what ended up being a disastrous night for the Falcons' defense. It's typically not a good thing when your third-level defender has to make all the plays, but make them, Hellams did, saving several explosive plays from the Chiefs' offense from becoming house calls.

short_comment: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.
long_comment: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

short_comment: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
long_comment: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

short_comment: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
long_comment: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
long_comment: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

short_comment: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
long_comment: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
long_comment: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
long_comment: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Henderson and the Falcons agreed to a two-year contract extension Friday.
long_comment: Per Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network, Henderson's extension is worth up to $20 million and includes $11 million guaranteed. Henderson has started at outside cornerback in each of his last six outings, and he was moved into the starting lineup after A.J. Terrell landed on injured reserve in late September due to a groin injury. Across eight regular-season games, Henderson has logged 41 tackles (32 solo), nine pass defenses, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Thomas and the Falcons agreed to a three-year extension worth up to $33 million Friday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
long_comment: The extension means Thomas -- a third-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2022 NFL Draft -- will be under contract with the Falcons through the 2029 season. The fifth-year pro has stepped into a larger role defensively this year due to the absences of James Pearce (back) and Jalon Walker (knee, IR), the former of whom missed the first eight games of the 2026 campaign while serving a suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Thomas has accumulated 25 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: The Ravens traded Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick to the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for Ryan Neuzil, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The move gives the Falcons additional depth at the guard position behind starters Chris Lindstrom and Matthew Bergeron. Vorhees -- a seventh-round selection of the Ravens in the 2023 NFL Draft -- started in all 17 regular-season games in 2025, but he's started in only two of five contests this year. He also missed two games in October while recovering from a foot injury.

short_comment: Madubuike (hamstring) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
long_comment: Madubuike was injured in Monday night's loss to the Chargers and has logged back-to-back DNPs to open Week 11 prep work. Veteran John Jenkins would likely see a spike in defensive snaps if Madubuike is unable to play Sunday against the Panthers.

short_comment: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Humphrey won't play Sunday against the Panthers after the defensive back made a derogatory comment about the city of Baltimore in an episode of his podcast released Wednesday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Minter noted that after holding "internal conversations," he and the Ravens' brain trust decided to deactivate Humphrey for Week 11. Per Hensley, Humphrey acknowledged after Wednesday's practice that he regretted the comments he made in the podcast and issued an apology, so he's not expected to face any discipline beyond being held out of the matchup with the Panthers. Through the Ravens' first 10 games, Humphrey has tallied 40 tackles, nine pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.

short_comment: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Ioane exited Monday's loss to the Chargers due to a shoulder injury and was unable to return to the contest. The rookie first-round pick showed enough improvement two days later to get back on the field in a limited capacity, which bodes well for his chances of playing Sunday against the Panthers.

short_comment: Hawkins (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Hawkins has missed the Ravens' last four games while working through a knee injury. He was able to log some limited practices during Week 10 prep, and if he can increase his practice participation over the next couple of days, then he would be on track to return for Week 11 against the Panthers on Sunday.

short_comment: The Ravens reinstated Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve Wednesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: With the rookie fifth-round pick's 21-day evaluation window coming to a close Wednesday, Baltimore added him to the 53-man roster to ensure that he'll be available to play over the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 240-pound Randall has been a full participant in practices since Week 8 and should be healthy enough to play Sunday at Carolina, but it's unclear if Baltimore will make him active for that contest. Randall will likely slot in third on the depth chart at running back behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Rasheen Ali is a key contributor on special teams who could be prioritized ahead of Randall on game days.

short_comment: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

short_comment: The Ravens believe "there's a chance" that Jackson (thumb) could return for their Week 16 matchup with the Browns, assuming all goes well in his recovery from right thumb surgery, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Last Friday, head coach Jesse Minter announced that Jackson was facing a projected recovery timeline of 6-to-10 weeks after requiring a procedure to address a broken and dislocated thumb. A Week 16 return would be right up against the short end of that timeline, so if Jackson has shown notable improvement by that point, he could push to play if the 4-6 Ravens haven't faded from the playoff picture. While Jackson remains sidelined for at least a few more weeks, the Ravens will entrust trade-deadline acquisition Jacoby Brissett to direct the offense.

short_comment: Smith finished Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers with eight tackles (six solo).
long_comment: Kyle Hamilton led Baltimore with 10 tackles, and Smith was among three players who finished second with eight stops apiece. The veteran linebacker has hit the eight-tackle mark in four straight games and in eight of his 10 contests overall this season. Smith is tied for 11th in the NFL with 82 tackles on the campaign.

short_comment: Hamilton posted 10 tackles (three solo) against the Chargers in Monday's Week 10 loss.
long_comment: Hamilton is managing a hip injury but played all but one of Baltimore's defensive snaps Monday. He led the team with 10 stops, which were the second-most he's recorded in a contest so far this season. Hamilton seems to be on his way to a third consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign, as he has 70 stops through 10 games on the season.

short_comment: Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.

short_comment: Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Patterson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
long_comment: Patterson was signed by the Ravens on Wednesday, and he was able to make a 26-yard field goal as time expired in the first half before later adding a 36-yard make in the third quarter. With Tyler Loop (groin) set to miss at least two more contests while on injured reserve, Patterson will likely remain the team's starting kicker for the time being.

short_comment: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
long_comment: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

short_comment: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

short_comment: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

short_comment: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
long_comment: According to Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site, Andrews confirmed after Monday's game that he's been playing through a broken left hand since Week 3, but he finally appears to be back to full health. Though he didn't miss any time due to broken hand, he was listed on the injury report from Weeks 4 through 9 before avoiding the report entirely for Week 10. He proceeded to deliver a season-best performance in starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett's team debut, eclipsing his previous-best mark in receiving yardage by 33 yards. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers, especially now that he appears to have fully healed up from the hand injury.

short_comment: Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour note. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.

short_comment: Brissett completed 33 of 49 passes for 340 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and added two rushes for two yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: Brissett looked like a natural fit in coordinator Declan Doyle's offense despite having only practiced a handful of days with the Ravens following his trade from the Cardinals, amassing his highest passing yardage total since Week 11 of last season. As he'd often done with Trey McBride in Arizona, Brissett focused heavily on the tight-end position in his Baltimore debut, connecting with Mark Andrews and Josh Cuevas a combined 11 times for 119 yards. Brissett recorded completions to seven different targets overall, but his one interception did lead to a Chargers touchdown. Brissett's prospects in this offense look bright if his first game is any indication, and he'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday.

short_comment: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
long_comment: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

short_comment: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback Monday night versus the Chargers.
long_comment: Slovis will operate as Baltimore's third option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Joe Fagnano are removed from the contest.

short_comment: Wiggins (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
long_comment: Wiggins was inactive for the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. However, after logging a full practice session Thursday, it appears he is good to go for Week 10 against the Chargers. The 23-year-old has appeared in eight games this season, garnering 24 total tackles (17 solo) and four passes defensed.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Thursday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Kincaid has now kicked off Week 11 prep with consecutive absences from practice, but he'll be able to erase some concern about his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins if he's able to get back on the field Friday in some capacity.

short_comment: Parker accumulated five tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Parker sacked his former Clemson quarterback Cade Klubnik twice in the Bills' blowout win. The rookie second-rounder called his shot, discussing his wishes to sack Klubnik while answering a question from Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo in late April.

short_comment: Alford (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough.
long_comment: Alford sustained a concussion during the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. The cornerback remains in the NFL's concussion protocol and will need to upgrade his practice participation as the week progresses. Alford also needs to be cleared by an independent neurologist ahead of Sunday's contest against the Dolphins for a chance to suit up during Week 11.

short_comment: Williams (calf) didn't participate in Buffalo's walkthrough Wednesday.
long_comment: Williams is still dealing with the calf injury that forced him to exit the Week 10 win over the Jets early. If the 2023 third-round pick ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup versus the Dolphins, Kaleb Elarms-Orr would be in line to start at inside linebacker in his place alongside Terrel Bernard.

short_comment: Benford (groin) was estimated as a nonparticipant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
long_comment: Benford exited the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets early with a groin injury and did not return to the contest. The star cornerback remains sidelined as he manages the issue. Benford will need to upgrade to at least a limited participant by Friday's practice session for a shot at avoiding an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

short_comment: Hawes (shoulder) was a late addition to Wednesday's injury report, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News.
long_comment: It is unclear whether Hawes suffered his shoulder injury, however, his eligibility for Week 11 against the Dolphins will likely be decided during the Thursday and Friday prep sessions. The 25-year-old will need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

short_comment: Bishop (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
long_comment: Bishop played all 65 defensive snaps in the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets after entering the weekend questionable with a groin injury. The free safety appears to have picked up a shoulder injury in the contest and has continued his streak of limited participation through Week 11. Bishop will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

short_comment: Hooker (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
long_comment: Hooker likely sustained his knee injury in the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. The strong safety played all 70 defensive snaps in his first game as a Bill, logging seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed in the contest. The trade deadline acquisition from the Titans will need to continue to log limited or full practice sessions through Friday for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

short_comment: Hamlin (toe) was estimated to be a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
long_comment: Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News spotted Hamlin in a walking boot during the limited session. The reserve free safety played 17 defensive snaps and 17 special-teams snaps in Sunday's win over the Jets, likely sustaining the toe injury in one of his 34 reps.

short_comment: Davis was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
long_comment: Davis is making his first appearance on the injury report since Week 8, when he missed a practice due to an illness. Unless the hamstring issue was something that resulted in him exiting Wednesday's session early, Davis should still have decent odds of being ready to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The third-year back has seen limited playing time behind James Cook and Ty Johnson this season, earning no more than six touches in any of his nine appearances to date.

short_comment: Bills head coach Joe Brady said Wednesday that Shavers (knee) has been reinstated from the PUP list, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
long_comment: Shavers' 21-day evaluation window was set to close this week, so the Bills elected to add him back to the 53-man roster to ensure that he would be available to play this season. The wideout has been a full practice participant for the past two weeks, so he appears to be fully recovered from the torn ACL he sustained in January and should be available for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If active for the Week 11 contest, Shavers will likely slot in as a depth option at receiver behind the trio of DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman.

short_comment: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.

short_comment: The Bills placed Reed-Adams (back) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: It's not immediately clear when he suffered the back injury, but Reed-Adams will now have to sit out at least four games as he recovers. His absence leaves veteran Austin Corbett as Buffalo's undisputed backup plan at guard behind starters Alec Anderson and O'Cyrus Torrence.

short_comment: Bass made his sole field-goal attempt and all four PATs in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Bass made a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker continues his perfect streak, having made all 20 of his field-goal attempts so far in 2026, with three such conversions coming from beyond 50 yards.

short_comment: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

short_comment: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

short_comment: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

short_comment: Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Moore's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter accounted for half of his team-high total in receiving yards. This was his most productive outing since Moore went for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and the veteran wide receiver has chipped in 216 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in three games since returning from a shoulder injury. Josh Allen and James Cook continue to lead Buffalo's offense with their legs, but Moore has re-established himself as Allen's top target in the passing game heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

short_comment: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.

short_comment: Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
long_comment: Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during the productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

short_comment: Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Both Tremble and Darren Waller (knee) were upgraded to limited work after being DNP on Wednesday. Friday's participation levels and injury designations will tell a better story for their Week 11 availability versus Baltimore. Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are next in line at tight end for Carolina.

short_comment: Brooks (groin) remained a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Brooks is still on injured reserve but appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Baltimore on Sunday. Chuba Hubbard should remain head-and-shoulders above Brooks on the depth chart as the clear RB1 for Carolina, but the Panthers likely also want to use the rest of the season to see if Brooks can stay healthy for a stretch and produce when given opportunities. Brooks is worth adding in fantasy, but his role will need to be defined before plugging him in lineups.

short_comment: Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN reports.
long_comment: One day removed from being a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, Waller was able to mix into some drills, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point his odds to suit up Sunday against the Ravens will become known.

short_comment: Lee (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Lee missed the Panthers' last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, his full participation in Wednesday's practice indicates that the rookie fourth-rounder has fully recovered from his injury, and Lee should be back on the field for the Panthers against the Ravens on Sunday.

short_comment: Okereke (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Okereke has been sidelined for each of the Panthers' last two games while recovering from a foot injury, which has also prevented him from practicing. He has two more chances to return to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's home game against the Ravens. Tyrel Dodson has stepped into a starting role at inside linebacker in Okereke's absence.

short_comment: Young was listed with a sore foot on Wednesday's injury report but was a full participant in the Panthers' first Week 11 practice.
long_comment: Per Steve Reed of the Associated Press, head coach Dave Canales said that Young experienced some soreness in his foot coming out of Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints. However, after receiving treatment over the last couple of days, Young responded well enough to take every rep in practice to kick off Week 11 prep. The signal-caller isn't expected to face any limitations during this Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Dodson logged seven tackles (two solo) Sunday in a 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: Dodson finished second on the Panthers in stops behind Devin Lloyd (nine). It was the second straight start for Dodson as a result of Bobby Okereke being sidelined by a foot injury. If Okereke can't return for this Sunday's matchup against Baltimore, Dodson would figure to start and handle an every-down role again.

short_comment: Lloyd registered nine tackles (five solo) and an interception in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: Lloyd was prolific as a tackler, leading Carolina with nine stops. He also put an end to the Saints' first offensive possession of the game with an interception of Tyler Shough. The pickoff was Lloyd's third of the campaign, a tally he's now reached in three of his five NFL seasons. With 63 tackles through eight contests, Lloyd is also on pace to reach triple-digit tackles for the fourth time.

short_comment: Legette didn't produce any output in the boxscore during Carolina's win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Legette made his return to the lineup after having been sidelined since Week 2 due to a knee injury, but he ended up playing just two snaps on offense. He will look to be more involved during next week's matchup versus the Ravens.

short_comment: Metchie caught his only target for four yards Sunday in a 20-17 win against New Orleans.
long_comment: Metchie's only catch and target came late in the third quarter, as he logged four yards on a third-down play to help set up a Ryan Fitzgerald field goal. The veteran wideout had a streak of six games with multiple catches snapped in the Carolina victory. Metchie finished third among Panthers wideouts with 23 offensive snaps, and he's produced like a No. 3 receiver this year, logging no more than three catches and 40 yards in any of his eight games to date.

short_comment: Etienne took three carries for one yard and caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans. He also returned three punts for 43 yards.
long_comment: Etienne again played second fiddle to starter Chuba Hubbard in Week 10 with Jonathon Brooks sidelined by a groin injury, and Etienne got his second-most touches of the season. His role on offense in Week 11 will depend on Brooks' status, but the vast majority of the Panthers' snaps at tailback will continue to go to Hubbard.

short_comment: Fitzgerald made two of his three field-goal attempts and both PATs in the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints on Sunday.
long_comment: Fitzgerald's 54-yard field goal as time expired iced the game for the Panthers. The kicker made another field goal from 55 yards while also missing his first attempt of the night from 48 yards out. Fitzgerald moves to 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts and 18-for-23 on PATs so far during the 2026 regular season.

short_comment: The Panthers signed Wilson from the practice squad to the active roster Monday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Wilson has started the last three games at cornerback as a practice-squad elevation, and the Panthers have now made room for him on the 53-man roster. Wilson is set to start Sunday's game against the Ravens at outside cornerback opposite Will Lee (hamstring) or Corey Thornton. The Panthers released linebacker Nick Hampton in a corresponding move.

short_comment: Coker failed to catch any of his four targets in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
long_comment: While it looked like Coker was going to be in line for a breakout 2026 season after his 8-138-2 receiving performance in the Week 1 opener, Coker has been held to 23 catches for 255 yards and one touchdown over his last seven games. At this point, he can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows something in the box score again. This was a pristine on-paper spot versus New Orleans in the dome, and next Sunday's home date against Baltimore won't be any easier.

short_comment: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
long_comment: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

short_comment: Hubbard carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught all five of his targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
long_comment: The 27-year-old RB kept the Panthers' offense afloat nearly single-handedly, as he set a new career high with 172 scrimmage yards while scoring both the team's TDs, on a two-yard run in the first quarter and a one-yard plunge in the fourth. Hubbard's 80 receiving yards were easily a new career high, topping the 3-57-0 line on three targets he recorded in Week 15 of the 2022 season against the Steelers. Over Hubbard's last six games, he surged to 697 scrimmage yards and six rushing touchdowns, and he'll look keep rolling in a Week 11 clash with the Ravens.

short_comment: Phillips (hamstring) is active against the Saints on Sunday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
long_comment: Phillips has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Prior to the injury, he accumulated 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks, across five regular-season games. His return will bolster the Panthers' pass rush alongside Patrick Jones, Trevis Gipson and Princely Umanmielen.

short_comment: Christensen (hamstring) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Christensen drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Saints after logging a trio of full practices. However, he's not quite ready to return from a hamstring injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Jackson (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Jackson's 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and he drew the doubtful tag for Sunday's game after logging a trio of limited sessions. He's not quite ready to return from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, and his next opportunity to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Stevenson (hand) was not listed on the Bears' estimated injury report Wednesday.
long_comment: Stevenson injured his hand during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Buccaneers. He had additional time to rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and given Stevenson's absence from Wednesday's estimated practice report, the fourth-year defensive back should suit up Sunday against the Saints. He has accumulated 34 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Gordon (shoulder) was estimated as a DNP on Wednesday's practice report.
long_comment: Gordon is working through a shoulder injury that he picked up during the Bears' Week 9 win over the Buccaneers. The Week 10 bye gave the fifth-year safety additional time to recover, and with the Bears not practicing Wednesday, Gordon's participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his status heading into Sunday's contest against the Saints.

short_comment: Simmons (knee) was listed as a limited practice participant on Wednesday's estimated report.
long_comment: The Bears are coming out of a bye for Week 10, so it appears that Simmons picked up the injury during Chicago's Week 9 win over Tampa Bay, when he logged four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense. Simmons has recorded a sack in each of his first two games with his new team, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.

short_comment: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate.
long_comment: Monangai told Courtney Cronin of ESPN on Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints, and after being spotted in full pads at Tuesday's unofficial practice, the running back would have logged an uncapped session one day later if the team had held drills. Monangai is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a turf toe injury and a right thumb concern.

short_comment: Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Tuesday that Burden has cleared concussion protocol, Patrick Finley of the Chicago Sun-Times reports.
long_comment: Burden's status was up in the air for a bit with the Bears going on bye immediately after he sustained a concussion in a Week 9 win over the  Buccaneers, but he was spotted working out on the field with teammates Monday and has apparently cleared all five phases of the protocol. The second-year wideout looks like he'll be a full practice participant throughout Week 11, and he shouldn't face any playing-time limitations in Sunday's game versus the Saints.

short_comment: Johnson recorded three tackles (one solo) and a pick-six during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.
long_comment: In a game that featured seven turnovers between the two teams, Johnson's takeaway was arguably the most impactful of them all. He jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Cade Otton late in the third quarter, which Johnson returned 67 yards to the house for the second pick-six of his NFL career. The veteran defensive back is up to 27 tackles (21 solo), three pass defenses (including a pick-six) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Lewis produced six tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers in Week 9.
long_comment: Lewis jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Tez Johnson late in the second quarter, although the Bears offense turned the ball over on the very next play. It was the first interception of the season for Lewis and second of his career. The veteran safety is up to 35 tackles (25 solo) and two pass defenses across eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Thomas hauled in one of his two targets for 13 yards and returned three kicks for 88 yards during Chicago's win versus Tampa Bay on Sunday.
long_comment: Thomas continues to see limited action offensively, playing just five snaps Sunday and no more than 15 on offense in any game this season, though he did manage to record his seventh reception of the season. The rookie third-round pick should continue to see the majority of his action come on special teams, and he's now amassed 715 kick-return yards across nine outings this season.

short_comment: Roush caught both of his two targets for 23 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

short_comment: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
long_comment: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

short_comment: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs.
long_comment: Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

short_comment: Santos made both of his two field-goal attempts and converted all three of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: It was an up-and-down night for Chicago's offense Sunday, as it moved the ball relatively well but committed five turnovers. Nevertheless, Santos got an opportunity to win the game on the last play of regulation with a 38-yard field goal, and it looked good from the moment it left his foot. Following a bye in Week 10, the Bears will play host to the Saints in Week 11, at which point fantasy managers might want to confirm the weather forecast in Chicago before locking Santos back into their lineups.

short_comment: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

short_comment: Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards and didn't catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Swift was bottled up by an elite Buccaneers run defense that came into Week 9 allowing a league-low 80 rushing yards per game. He nearly had a fumble in the fourth quarter but was ruled down by contact on a play that the Buccaneers unsuccessfully challenged. Swift's momentum came to an abrupt halt with this season-worst performance, as he failed to reach 70 scrimmage yards for the first time all season after racking up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games. After Chicago's Week 10 bye, Swift could be back to sharing the backfield with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who hasn't played since Week 4 but recently returned to practice.

short_comment: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards.
long_comment: Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Keenum (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Bears' emergency No. 3 quarterback for Sunday Night Football versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: Keenum will once again operate as the team's emergency QB option in Week 9, making it four games in a row in that role. The 38-year-old will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent are forced out of the contest.

short_comment: Jarrett (groin) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.
long_comment: After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.

short_comment: The Bears placed Scott (wrist) on injured reserve Thursday.
long_comment: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

short_comment: The Bears placed Street (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday, Adam Jahns of AllCHGO.com reports.
long_comment: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

short_comment: Iosivas (thumb) practiced fully Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Iosivas had his 21-day practice window opened last week but remains on injured reserve. With Dohnte Meyers playing well as the Bengals' WR3, there's likely no rush to activate Iosivas, who has just 87 career regular-season catches across 52 appearances. He's averaged 20.2 receiving yards per game in his career.

short_comment: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Burrow (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: After appearing on the injury report with an illness, Burrow's full practice Thursday suggests the Bengals quarterback isn't facing any obvious limitations ahead of Monday night's date with the Commanders. A frontrunner in the MVP conversation, Burrow has been playing lights-out football for the past month-plus, as he and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are firing on all cylinders.

short_comment: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.
long_comment: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.

short_comment: Battle finished Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh with six tackles (four solo), one defensed pass and one forced fumble.
long_comment: Battle ranked second on Cincinnati in stops. One of his six tackles went for a loss, and the 25-year-old also forced a fumble, though it was recovered by the Steelers. Battle has played every defensive snap in seven of the Bengals' nine contests this season, and he's collected 58 tackles and eight defensed passes, including three interceptions.

short_comment: Knight finished with eight tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass against the Steelers in a 38-18 victory Sunday.
long_comment: Knight led Cincinnati in tackles in the blowout win. The second-year linebacker has recorded exactly eight stops in four of his past five games, and he's finished with at least that tally in all but three of his appearances overall this season. Knight hasn't yet recorded a sack, but he's on pace to blow by his rookie total of 106 stops, as he has 71 tackles across nine games.

short_comment: Carter posted six tackles (two solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Carter's tackle tally tied for second-most on the Bengals. The second-year pro has now reached the six-tackle mark in all but one of his nine games this season. Carter leads the Bengals with 74 stops overall, and he's recorded 1.5 sacks, five defensed passes (including an interception) and two forced fumbles.

short_comment: Sample caught all three of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-18 win against Pittsburgh.
long_comment: Sample entered the contest with no catches over his previous two games, but he tied season-high marks in both receptions and targets versus the Steelers. He gave Cincinnati a two-score lead just after the beginning of the second quarter when he hauled in a three-yard TD from Joe Burrow. Sample has two touchdowns over his past four games, but with just five catches for 39 yards during that span, he's almost entirely dependent on getting into the end zone to generate useful fantasy production.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: McPherson made one of his two field-goal attempts and all five PATs in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: McPherson converted a 24-yard field-goal attempt on the first drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to miss a 43-yarder in the second quarter of the contest, though the miss did not end up mattering to the final result of the game. McPherson is now 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts and 33-for-33 on PATs over nine contests this season.

short_comment: Meyers caught both of his targets for 20 yards and a touchdown while also adding 58 yards as a kick returner during Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: Meyers reeled in multiple passes for the third straight game, and he was able to secure his first score of the year in the second quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow. The 26-year-old's 28 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Cincinnati behind Ja'Marr Chase (59), Tee Higgins (51) and Colbie Young (29). With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) nearing a return to action, Meyers may see a sharp drop in offensive opportunities in the near future.

short_comment: Perine turned six carries into 14 yards and a touchdown and hauled in all four of his targets for 25 yards during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: It looked like Chase Brown found the end zone in the fourth quarter for his third score of the game, but replay assist revealed that his knee came down just short of the goal line. Perine came in on the next play and took the ball for a one-yard touchdown to extend the Bengals' lead to 38-10 following Evan MacPherson's successful extra-point try. It was Perine's third touchdown of the season and first since Week 7 against the Ravens, and over his last five games, he has turned 39 carries into 151 yards (3.9 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding seven catches on as many targets for 44 yards and a score. He'll continue to operate as the Bengals' RB2 behind Brown heading into Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.

short_comment: Brooks carried three times for 12 yards while taking the field for three of the Bengals' 66 offensive snaps in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: All three of Brooks' carries came during the Bengals' final possession of the fourth quarter, when the team had already built a sizable lead and opted to rest multiple key players, including top running back Chase Brown. Brooks has been active for all nine of the Bengals' games to date but has logged just six carries, all of which have come late in blowout victories. So long as Brown and Samaje Perine are both available, Brooks will continue to see limited playing time on offense.

short_comment: Gesicki caught one pass for nine yards in Sunday night's 38-18 win over the Steelers.
long_comment: Gesicki caught six touchdowns in the first seven games of the season, but he's now produced just three grabs for 20 scoreless yards over the past two contests. The fluky touchdown rate was never going to hold up, and Joe Burrow funnels so many of his targets through Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown that there isn't a whole lot more to go around to Cincinnati's ancillary weapons. Gesicki is a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks despite running a bunch of routes as the de facto slot receiver.

short_comment: Brown rushed 10 times for 44 yards and brought in eight of nine targets for 39 yards for two touchdowns in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
long_comment: Brown averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry, but as is customary, his rushing opportunities were capped in a Bengals offense that typically takes a pass-heavy approach irrespective of game script. He still benefited from that philosophy, however, as he tied his second-highest reception total on the season while ending his seven-game touchdown drought by hitting paydirt twice. Brown will get another favorable opportunity to build on his production in Week 11, when the Bengals travel to D.C. for a matchup with the Commanders.

short_comment: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati.
long_comment: Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.

short_comment: Burks (groin) will not return to Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
long_comment: Prior to leaving, Burks recorded a pair of solo tackles. He's primarily played on special teams this season. Jack Kiser will be in line for increased reps with Burks sidelined.

short_comment: Risner (knee) will not return to Sunday night's game against the Steelers.
long_comment: The veteran right guard was injured in the first half, and with the Bengals already stomping Pittsburgh, there's no need to push Risner back out there. It'll remain to be seen if he's looking at a multigame absence. Jalen Rivers has replaced Risner on the offensive line.

short_comment: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
long_comment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.

short_comment: The Bengals opened Parker's (undisclosed) 21-day practice window Thursday.
long_comment: Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

short_comment: Campbell logged five tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including one interception, in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.

short_comment: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.

short_comment: Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.

short_comment: Wallace caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Texans. He also recorded one tackle in kick coverage.
long_comment: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: Szmyt made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

short_comment: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

short_comment: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.

short_comment: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

short_comment: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.
long_comment: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

short_comment: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
long_comment: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

short_comment: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland.
long_comment: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Fannin led the Browns across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 30-yard grab on Cleveland's penultimate possession set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning five-yard touchdown rush on the next play. Fannin's chemistry with Deshaun Watson has been outstanding, and the second-year tight end now has at least 91 receiving yards in three of the past four games. Fannin will remain a central figure in Cleveland's impressive air attack when the team returns to action in a home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Judkins rushed 10 times for 38 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of five targets for 33 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
long_comment: Judkins' rushing volume was at a season-low level, but the second-year back managed to record his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a five-yard run with just under a minute remaining. That proved to be the game-winning score, and Judkins also mustered his second-highest receiving yardage tally of the campaign. The 2025 first-round pick is averaging just 3.4 yards per carry, however, so he remains far from efficient heading into a Week 11 bye ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Barnett (hamstring) has returned to Sunday's game against Houston, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
long_comment: Barnett left in the first quarter due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran defensive lineman was cleared by medical staff to return to Sunday's contest.

short_comment: The Browns placed Burton (calf) on injured reserve Saturday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
long_comment: Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

short_comment: Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Houston.
long_comment: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Ward (quadriceps) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Ward was managing a quad injury during all of Week 10 prep, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's game despite not logging a full practice. The veteran defensive back has 34 tackles (19 solo), nine pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

long_comment: questionable

long_comment: questionable

short_comment: The Cowboys designated Thompson (hamstring) for return to practice from injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Per Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site, Thompson was a limited participant at practice Wednesday. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which Dallas can officially activate him before he'd have to go back to IR for the rest of the season.

short_comment: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

short_comment: Turpin caught one of three targets for 10 yards Sunday in a Week 10 loss to San Francisco. He also rushed once for nine yards.
long_comment: Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times in the offensive slugfest, but Turpin got only three of his targets. Meanwhile, George Pickens drew a whopping 18 looks, CeeDee Lamb got 13 and Ryan Flournoy got seven, and all three of those wideouts scored at least one touchdown. Turpin logged a 17 percent offensive snap share in his return from a three-game absence caused by an injury to his ribs. He's fallen below a 20 percent offensive snap share in all but one of his seven appearances this season, so Turpin seems to be steadfastly locked into no higher than Dallas' No. 4 wideout role.

short_comment: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.
