short_comment: Aubrey made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Aubrey connected on 52-yard field goals in both the first and third quarters, although his PAT in the second missed wide left. It was the second missed extra-point try of the season for Aubrey and his seventh miss overall, although five of those failed kicks have come on field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards. The Cowboys will stay home for Week 11 against the Titans, who give up 26.6 points per game (27th in the NFL) and have yielded 40-plus points in each of their last two contests.

short_comment: Abanikanda reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
long_comment: Abanikanda made his 2026 regular-season debut against the 49ers in Week 10, when he operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams. Abanikanda finished that contest with two carries for eight yards and a two-yard catch on his lone target in what ended as a 46-40 loss for Dallas. With both Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) on injured reserve, Abanikanda figures to be elevated to the Cowboys' active roster for Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday.

short_comment: Bland sustained a high-ankle sprain in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Bland will likely miss time after suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 10 against the 49ers. It's unclear how much time he'll be sidelined, but the injury could be related to an issue that plagued Bland during the practice week. Cobie Durant will likely fill in for Bland should the standout cornerback miss any time.

short_comment: Booker suffered a high-ankle sprain in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News  reports.
long_comment: Booker is expected to miss multiple weeks after injuring his ankle in the first half of Sunday's game against the 49ers, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. The 22-year-old may be able to avoid being placed on injured reserve with the Cowboys' bye coming in Week 14. T.J. Bass will likely slot into Booker's right guard spot.

short_comment: Williams rushed 16 times for 63 yards and brought in his only target for four yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Williams had a near monopoly on the Cowboys' running back touches, but he worked hard for everything he got against a talented 49ers front seven. The veteran back averaged under 4.0 yards per carry for the seventh time this season, but he did eclipse 60 rushing yards for the third time in the last four games. Williams will take 692 rushing yards and nine rush TDs -- along with a 25-131-1 receiving line -- into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

short_comment: Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.

short_comment: Prescott completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards with five touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for seven yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also ran for a two-point conversion.
long_comment: Playing catch-up from the second quarter on did wonders for Prescott's fantasy production, as the veteran quarterback sent 38 total targets in the direction of the talented trio of George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy alone. Prescott connected with Pickens for three of his scoring strikes, which went for 35, 39 and five yards. Flournoy (11 yards) and Lamb (one yard) accounted for the final two in the fourth quarter, and Prescott added a two-point conversion run after the final scoring toss with an admirable diving attempt on which he made contact with the pylon with the extended ball. Prescott tied a career high with his TD pass total, while his passing yardage was a season high. He should have an opportunity to put together a successful encore next Sunday, as a Week 11 home matchup with the vulnerable Titans secondary awaits.

short_comment: Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
long_comment: After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

short_comment: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble.
long_comment: Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

short_comment: Ogbonnia (finger) has re-entered Sunday's matchup against San Francisco, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
long_comment: Ogbonnia suffered a finger injury in the second quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to get back on the field after halftime. Ogbonnia will thus continue to play a key role along Dallas' defensive line.

short_comment: Bullard (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The Cowboys activated Bullard from injured reserve Saturday. The defensive tackle has been sidelined since sustaining a calf injury during the Cowboys' Week 3 loss to the Ravens. Bullard is set to suit up as a rotational defensive lineman behind starter Otito Ogbonnia.

short_comment: Porter (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Porter upgraded to limited participation in Friday's practice after missing the first two Week 10 prep sessions and the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. The cornerback is all set to return to the field alongside DaRon Bland to anchor the Cowboys' secondary for a big matchup with one of the NFC's top contenders.

short_comment: The Cowboys signed Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: The Cowboys technically still have one elevation to use on Mitchell this season, but they instead will opt to sign him to the active roster for Week 10. His signing gives the Cowboys extra depth at tight end, as the team will be without Jake Ferguson (knee) for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

short_comment: Waddle (concussion) was a full practice participant Thursday.
long_comment: A full practice participant for the second day in a row, Waddle looks to be close to clearing the NFL's concussion protocol after he sustained the head injury in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers. Assuming he can receive clearance from an independent neurologist by the weekend, Waddle will be removed from the protocol and suit up Sunday versus the Raiders.

short_comment: Moss (concussion) signed a four-year contract extension with the Broncos on Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, the deal is worth $67 million and keeps Moss on the Broncos' books through 2030. A 2023 third-round draft pick, Moss has started in all 39 of his appearances over his first three-plus seasons in Denver and leads the NFL with 19 pass breakups since the start of the 2025 campaign, per Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com. With 2024 NFL Defensive Player of the Year Pat Surtain under contract through 2029, the Broncos should have one of the league's top cornerback tandems in place for the next several seasons. Moss is currently listed on the Broncos' Week 11 injury report while he recovers from a concussion sustained in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers, but he was a full participant Wednesday and looks likely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

short_comment: Jones (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Jones was unable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers due to a hamstring injury that he picked up against the Cowboys in Week 8. He's had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 10 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

short_comment: Prentice (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: It appears Prentice entered the league's concussion protocol following the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers. He had additional time to recover courtesy of the Week 10 bye, so the veteran fullback should be available for Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders.

short_comment: Hufanga (ankle) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
long_comment: Wednesday was Hufanga's first full practice since he hurt his ankle back in Week 5 against the Chargers. Barring any setbacks, it looks like he'll have a good chance to return to game action Sunday versus the Raiders.

short_comment: The Broncos opened Lohner's (lower body) 21-day practice window Wednesday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
long_comment: Lohner opened the season on injured reserve after undergoing a procedure on his lower body in June. It appears the 25-year-old could make his return soon, as the Broncos have 21 days to officially activate him from IR before he becomes ineligible to return in 2026.

short_comment: Singleton recorded six tackles (two solo) during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers in Week 9.
long_comment: Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.

short_comment: Trautman caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

short_comment: Mims caught one of two targets for zero yards, added a five-yard carry and returned three punts for 22 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

short_comment: Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
long_comment: Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.

short_comment: Lutz went 2-for-2 on both his field-goal attempts and extra-point tries during Denver's win over Carolina on Sunday.
long_comment: Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.

short_comment: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
long_comment: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

short_comment: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
long_comment: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

short_comment: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

short_comment: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
long_comment: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

short_comment: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries.
long_comment: The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

short_comment: Tillman is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Tillman was on the injury report ahead of the Week 9 meeting with Carolina due to a hamstring issue. However, he will avoid his second absence of the 2026 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven games for the Broncos this season, amassing 19 total tackles (10 solo).

short_comment: The Broncos placed Uwazurike (shoulder) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
long_comment: Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

short_comment: Vaki (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
long_comment: A limited participant for Wednesday's walkthrough, Vaki continued to operate with some restrictions while the Lions held a more traditional practice Thursday. Vaki's involvement in any capacity is nonetheless a good sign for his Week 11 status, though he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers.

short_comment: McCreary recorded six tackles (four solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: McCreary recorded his first interception of the season in Week 10, when he jumped in front of a pass from Tommy DeVito -- who took over under center for the Patriots after Drake Maye injured his ankle in the first quarter -- that was intended for Mack Hollins, although the Lions' offense couldn't convert the takeaway into points. McCreary is up to 38 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, 10 pass defenses and one forced fumble across nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Reed (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
long_comment: A hip injury has prevented Reed from playing in each of the Lions' last two games, and the veteran defensive back expressed pessimism Wednesday about his ability to suit up for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, per Jeremy Reisman of PrideofDetroit.com. If Reed doesn't play in Week 11, then Khalil Dorsey (ankle) would likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback.

short_comment: The Lions activated Joseph (knee) from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday.
long_comment: Joseph was a full participant in his return to the active roster Wednesday. The free safety is set to make his 2026 debut in Week 11 against the Buccaneers, finally reuniting with strong safety Brian Branch after both spent lengthy periods on the Lions' reserve lists.

short_comment: The Lions placed Hutchinson (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Hutchinson's move to IR was merely a formality after he was diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee following his early exit from this past Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft has now succumbed to two season-ending injuries through his first five years in the league, after a fractured tibia and fibula in his left leg cut short his 2024 campaign.

long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Conklin went without a target while playing 22 of the Lions' 71 offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: A healthy inactive for two of the Lions' first four games of the season, Conklin has now suited up for five consecutive contests. However, the veteran tight end has been handling a limited role, logging less than one-third of the offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances on the season while compiling a 2-11-0 receiving line on three targets.

short_comment: Saylors rushed twice for nine yards while adding 26 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
long_comment: Saylors played six snaps on offense while serving as a No. 3 option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in the backfield. Saylors was on the field for 20 snaps with the special-teams unit, and he'll continue to be primarily a special-teams asset in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Wright caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Wright tied season highs in both receiving yards and catches during Sunday's win, and his 39 snaps on offense were second-most among Lions tight ends behind Sam LaPorta (56). Wright has accumulated seven catches on eight target for 42 yards across nine regular-season games, and he's mostly served as a blocking tight end on the Lions' offense.

short_comment: Mays (ankle) isn't expected to return to action Sunday versus Tampa Bay, Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press reports.
long_comment: Mays has already missed two contests due to an ankle injury he suffered Week 8 versus Minnesota. Head coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday that Mays is probably going to be out again this Sunday against the Bucs. That means Juice Scruggs will likely make another start at center for Detroit.

short_comment: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
long_comment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Williams caught four of seven targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs monopolized the Lions' offense on the day, scoring four of the team's five TDs, and there wasn't much production left over for Williams. The fifth-year wideout has topped 50 receiving yards just three times this season, and he'll take a 32-518-5 line on 51 targets through nine games into a Week 11 battle with the Buccaneers.

short_comment: St. Brown caught four of five targets for 98 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich.
long_comment: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early. St. Brown took full advantage of the volume he saw however, scoring on a 56-yard catch and run in the first quarter and then taking another short pass from Jared Goff and turning it into a 28-yard TD in the third. It was St. Brown's third multi-TD game of the season but his first since Week 2, and he'll take a 65-755-7 line on 91 targets through nine games into a Week 11 clash with the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Bates made all five of his PATs in the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Bates did not attempt a field goal in the contest. He remains 16-for-17 on field-goal attempts and moves to 29-for-29 on PATs through nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: TeSlaa caught two of five targets for 19 yards and a touchdown during the Lions' 35-10 win over the Patriots on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle.
long_comment: It was a quiet day for TeSlaa, with the Lions' offense being powered by usual suspects Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs, with the latter duo combining for four touchdowns (three receiving, one rushing). TeSlaa was the other Lions player to find the end zone, which took place early in the second quarter on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff. It was the first touchdown catch of the season for TeSlaa, who found the end zone six times across 17 regular-season games during his rookie campaign in 2025. He has been the Lions' distant WR3 behind St. Brown and Jameson Williams, and that shouldn't change ahead of the team's Week 11 tilt against the Buccaneers on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Gibbs carried the ball 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns while catching seven of eight targets for 99 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots.
long_comment: Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game early for New England, setting the stage for the rout, and Gibbs took full advantage as he set new season highs in receiving yards and scrimmage yards. It's the fourth time in 2026 that the star RB has topped 150 rushing yards, and his fourth game with multiple TDs. Gibbs has amassed 1,384 scrimmage yards and 13 total touchdowns through nine contests as he gets ready to face a stingy Buccaneers run defense in Week 11.

short_comment: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
long_comment: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

short_comment: Wonnum (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
long_comment: Wonnum entered the league's concussion protocol during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. He was held out of Detroit's Week 9 win over Miami, but Wonnum has cleared protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return bolsters the Lions' rotational depth on the defensive line alongside Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy and Derrick Moore.

short_comment: Williams logged eight tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.
long_comment: Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

short_comment: McKinney registered six tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.
long_comment: McKinney picked off a deep pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, although the Packers' offense failed to turn that takeaway into points before the end of the half. McKinney has three picks over his last two outings and is up to a league-leading six interceptions. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
long_comment: Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

long_comment: out

short_comment: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

short_comment: Brooks rushed two times for one yard and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.

short_comment: Sturdivant caught two passes for 37 yards and a touchdown on four targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: After Green Bay was shut out in the first half, Sturdivant's first career touchdown came in the third quarter from 32 yards out, and it went down as the Packers' lone touchdown of the afternoon. Sturdivant played just nine offensive snaps as the fourth receiver and would need more than one injury ahead of him on the depth chart to be relevant in fantasy.

short_comment: Smack went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Cisse (ribs) is "fine" after exiting the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings early, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Cisse did not return to Sunday's contest after exiting the game during the first quarter with a rib injury. Coach Matt LaFleur says the cornerback is "fine," and it appears Cisse will return to practice after the Packers' Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Moore's ankle injury is not considered serious, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

short_comment: Head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that Parsons (knee/illness) could be ready to make his season debut following the Packers' Week 11 bye, but he still has "a couple more hurdles" to clear before being deemed ready to play, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
long_comment: Since opening Parsons' 21-day practice window Nov. 4, the Packers have seemingly targeted their Nov. 25 matchup with the Rams in Week 12 for the star pass rusher's 2026 debut. That plan doesn't appear to have changed while Parsons has been a limited participant in practice for the past two weeks, but he'll likely need to start practicing in full during Week 12 prep before the Packers give him the green light to play. If Parsons does in fact gain clearance to play against the Rams, he could be operating with a restricted snap count in what would mark his first game action since tearing his left ACL on Dec. 14, 2025.

short_comment: Taylor completed one of two pass attempts for three yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: Down 20 points with four minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and with starting quarterback Jordan Love having already taken eight sacks on the afternoon, the Packers opted to turn to Taylor to direct the offense for their final possession of the day. All three of Taylor's appearances on the season have now come late in blowout wins or losses, and his opportunities are likely to remain limited to garbage-time situations so long as Love is healthy.

short_comment: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.
long_comment: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

short_comment: Johnson carried the ball 10 times for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

short_comment: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.

short_comment: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

short_comment: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
long_comment: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
long_comment: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

short_comment: Melton (thigh) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

short_comment: Glover (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
long_comment: Glover's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a knee injury that prevented him from playing against the Patriots in Week 9. The third-year pro was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he should reclaim his starting role at right guard from Laken Tomlinson.

short_comment: Van Ness (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Van Ness upgraded to limited in Friday's practice while dealing with a back injury. The weakside linebacker has recovered enough to suit up for Sunday's contest against a Vikings team that is also fighting for the NFC North title.

short_comment: Bullard (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
long_comment: Bullard was upgraded to a limited participant in Friday's practice and is questionable ahead of Sunday's contest. The starting slot cornerback is all set to suit up, seemingly having overcome his ankle injury in time for a heavyweight NFC North bout with the Vikings.

short_comment: Stewart is expected to move into a reserve safety role for Thursday night's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: The Texans are reinserting Reed Blankenship in the starting lineup after he returned from a broken hand and concussion Sunday against the Browns to play only two defensive snaps. Stewart recorded 14 tackles (four solo) in the loss but gave up a long reception to Jerry Jeudy in coverage. The Texans are looking for answers to get their defense back near the top of the league.

short_comment: Blankenship is expected to move back into the defensive starting lineup Thursday night against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: The safety missed two games with a broken hand and concussion before returning last Sunday against the Browns. He played just two defensive snaps versus Cleveland and logged 12 on special teams, but the Texans are swapping Blankenship back in at safety ahead of M.J. Stewart. Blankenship has 47 tackles (26 solo) and three pass breakups, including an interception, across seven appearances this season.

short_comment: Hutchinson is expected to continue to benefit from elevated playing time Thursday against the Colts while Marvin Harrison (hamstring) is sidelined for a second straight game, Jared Koch of SI.com reports.
long_comment: Harrison hasn't exceeded a 50 percent snap share in any of his three appearances with the Texans since coming over in a trade with the Cardinals, but his absence for the Week 10 loss to the Browns still proved beneficial for Hutchinson. The fourth-year wideout out of Iowa State tied his season high with nine targets against the Browns, finishing with four catches for 58 yards and a touchdown while playing more than three-fourths of the offensive snaps for a second consecutive contest. Another healthy snap share should await Hutchinson in Week 11, and he could represent the No. 2 option in the Houston passing game behind top target Nico Collins.

short_comment: Hummel (groin) is questionable for Houston's matchup against Indianapolis on Thursday.
long_comment: Hummel is still dealing with lingering effects of the groin injury that sidelined him from Week 1 until Week 10. The 26-year-old should still have a good chance of suiting up for Thursday's game, however, given he managed to play through the injury during last week's loss to the Browns.

short_comment: Smith (hamstring) is listed questionable for Thursday's game versus the Colts.
long_comment: Smith has been a full participant across the last four practices since being designated for return from injured reserve last week. He remains on IR, but with Houston listing him as questionable, Smith could be activated shortly before Thursday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. A second-year defensive back out of USC, Smith tallied two tackles over four games before landing on IR on Oct. 6.

short_comment: Lassiter (wrist) does not have any injury designation ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
long_comment: Lassiter did not participate in Tuesday' walkthrough due to a wrist issue. The cornerback sandwiched the DNP between two full sessions and has been cleared to play in Thursday night's contest. If Lassiter must see fewer snaps in the game as he manages the issue, Ja'Marcus Ingram could see the field opposite Derek Stingley.

short_comment: Hunter (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
long_comment: Hunter will now miss consecutive contests due to a hamstring injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The pass rusher was unable to practice during Week 11 prep as he continues to deal with the issue. Jadeveon Clowney is set to start at defensive end opposite Will Anderson for Thursday's AFC South showdown.

short_comment: Jordan (foot/illness) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
long_comment: Jordan missed all three Week 11 practice sessions due to an injury and an illness. The tight end will miss a second straight game, this time with two separate issues as opposed to the finger injury that plagued him ahead of Week 10. Marlin Klein or Cade Stover is set to be the No. 3 tight end behind Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau for Thursday night's contest.

short_comment: Demercado is expected to serve as the top complement to David Montgomery in Thursday's game against the Colts, with Woody Marks (concussion) ruled out for the contest.
long_comment: With Montgomery sidelined for a fourth straight game this past Sunday against the Browns and with Marks making an early exit, Demercado saw his most playing time of the season in the 27-24 loss. Demercado did little to capitalize on the opportunity, finishing with 15 yards from scrimmage on eight touches (seven carries, one reception). Though Marks wasn't able to clear concussion protocol in a short week, Montgomery has been cleared to play after he was listed as a full practice participant Monday through Wednesday. Montgomery should step back in as the Texans' preferred option out of the backfield, leaving Demercado to settle for more of a change-of-pace role.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Colts.
long_comment: Harrison was also inactive for this past Sunday's game against the Browns, and he will now target a potential return to action Nov. 29 versus the Ravens following Houston's Week 11 bye. In his continued absence, Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell will handle the Texans' WR duties Thursday. Collins (16 targets, nine catches) and Hutchinson (nine targets, four catches) combined for 152 receiving yards on the 25 targets the duo saw against Cleveland in Week 10.

short_comment: Marks (concussion) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Colts.
long_comment: After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns, Marks will be sidelined for the first time this season after he was unable to practice in any capacity on a short week. The second-year player had been operating as the Texans' clear lead back over the past four contests, but for at least one week, those duties are expected to fall to David Montgomery (groin), who has been cleared to return to action following a four-game absence. Once Marks clears the protocol, he could be form a timeshare with Montgomery.

short_comment: Montgomery (groin) doesn't have an injury designation and is expected to play in Thursday's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: Montgomery was sidelined for the Texans' past four games due to the groin injury, but he's good to go for the Week 11 matchup after he was listed as a full practice participant from Monday through Wednesday. Before going down with the injury, Montgomery had been part of a timeshare with Woody Marks, but Montgomery will have a fairly clear path to a lead role Thursday with Marks sidelined due to a concussion. Montgomery made a splash in his Texans debut with three touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bills, but he accrued just 126 scoreless yards on 36 touches (32 carries, four receptions) across his subsequent four contests prior to the four-game absence.

short_comment: To'oTo'o finished Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns with seven tackles (two solo).
long_comment: To'oTo'o was one of five Texans players who played every single defensive snap during Sunday's loss. In his four outings since returning in Week 6 from a four-game absence due to a shoulder injury, To'oTo'o has amassed 28 tackles (12 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble.

short_comment: Anderson posted four tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble during the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Despite not practicing during Week 10 prep due to an ankle injury, Anderson was cleared to play Sunday and was on the field for 54 of the Texans' 68 defensive snaps (79.4 percent). He strip-sacked Deshaun Watson on the last play of the second quarter, and Anderson is now up to a league-leading 10.5 sacks through nine regular-season games. He's currently the only player in the league with double-digit sacks heading into Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Colts, and Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones' 25 sacks are tied for sixth-most in the NFL.

short_comment: Hansen posted 12 tackles (four solo) during Houston's 27-24 loss to Cleveland on Sunday.
long_comment: Hansen was on the field for 66 of the Texans' 68 defensive snaps (97.1 percent) during Sunday's loss. His 12 tackles tied a career high he set in Week 4 against the Cowboys, and he finished second on the Texans in tackles behind M.J. Stewart (14). Hansen's playing time has fluctuated this season, but he figures to see more consistent snaps on defense for as long as Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) is on injured reserve. Hansen will head into Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Colts with 51 tackles (22 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including an interception) across nine regular-season games.

short_comment: Boutte failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
long_comment: Even with Marvin Harrison (hamstring) out and Jaylin Noel (toe) done for the season, Boutte was targeted on just one of C.J. Stroud's 38 pass attempts versus Cleveland. Boutte's 47 snaps on offense were fewer than both Nico Collins (57) and Xavier Hutchinson (51) but 14 more than Tank Dell, though Dell out-targeted Boutte four to one. Boutte popped off for 4-125-2 in Week 9 against the Chargers but otherwise has failed to reach 40 receiving yards in any of his eight other appearances this season.

short_comment: Fairbairn converted his sole field-goal attempt and made all three PATs in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Fairbairn's 45-yard field goal came in the first quarter, before the Texans blew a 17-point lead. The kicker is now 19-for-20 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 24-for-24 on PATs through nine regular-season contests in 2026.

short_comment: Ogunbowale reverted to the Texans' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
long_comment: Ogunbowale was elevated to the active roster to operate as a depth option in the backfield behind Woody Marks (concussion) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. The running back rushed one time for two yards while reeling in his only target for 13 yards in the defeat. With Marks potentially sidelined with a concussion and David Montgomery (groin) uncertain for Week 11, Ogunbowale could be elevated again ahead of Thursday night's matchup with the Colts.

short_comment: Rutledge (neck) was a full participant in Monday's walkthrough practice.
long_comment: Rutledge was unable to participate in any Week 10 prep sessions due to a neck injury and then sat out Sunday's loss to the Browns. Rutledge's estimated return to practice is a good sign for the first-round rookie's chances of playing in Thursday night's divisional showdown against the Colts.

short_comment: Al-Shaair (groin) did not participate in Monday's walkthrough practice.
long_comment: Al-Shaair was unable to play in Sunday's loss to the Browns due to a groin injury and personal matters. It had been unclear which issue contributed more to the middle linebacker's inability to practice in Week 10, but Monday's walkthrough provides further insight. Al-Shaair is clearly still suffering from the groin injury, and his status for the Texans' Thursday night showdown with the Colts remains uncertain.

short_comment: Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
long_comment: While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

short_comment: Dell brought in three of four targets for 21 yards and rushed once for no gain in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: One week after posting a 105-yard effort against the Chargers in only his second game since 2024, Dell saw a big downturn in yardage Sunday. Nevertheless, the fact he retained a solid complementary role was encouraging, and the speedy wideout seems to be playing unencumbered by any physical or mental limitations following the recovery from his devastating knee injury. Dell will look to boost his yardage back up in a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Stroud completed 20 of 38 passes for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception while adding three rushes for 20 yards in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Stroud looked like he was on his way to another highly productive day early while helping stake the Texans to a 17-0 lead in the first half, but the fourth-year signal-caller and his offense largely stagnated in the second half. Stroud spread the ball around while connecting with eight different targets overall, and his trio of scoring strikes went to Nico Collins (12 yards), Xavier Hutchinson (11 yards) and Dalton Schultz (11 yards), the latter accounting for Houston's only second-half points. Despite the Texans' monumental collapse, Stroud's highly impressive season continues, as he's up to 2,462 passing yards, a 19:3 TD:INT and 120 rushing yards and another score heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: Collins secured nine of 16 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Sunday.
long_comment: Collins comfortably paced the Texans across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and he added his fifth touchdown of the season on a 12-yard catch in the first quarter. Collins also had a 16-yard reception on Houston's last-gasp drive wiped out by an offensive holding penalty, but he still finished with season highs in receptions and targets. Collins retains an unquestioned No. 1 role in the Texans' prolific air attack, affording him an enticing combination of floor and upside heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Colts on Thursday night.

short_comment: According to Jane Slater of NFL Network, Gardner (calf) is not in line to play Thursday night against the Texans.
long_comment: Gardner is officially listed as questionable for the contest after being listed as a 'DNP' from Monday through Wednesday. His reported looming absence represents a hit to the Colts' Week 11 secondary that will be contending with the WR trio of Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell on Thursday. Official confirmation of the cornerback's availability will, in any case, arrive once Indy's inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 pm ET kickoff.

short_comment: Travis (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Travis will be sidelined for a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Cowboys, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29. Matt Goncalves figures to draw a second-straight start at right tackle in Travis' absence.

short_comment: Tillery (calf) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game at Houston.
long_comment: Tillery will be sidelined for a second consecutive contest as he deals with a lingering calf injury. In his absence, 2025 sixth-rounder Tim Smith should continue to see an expanded role at defensive tackle in Week 11.

short_comment: The Colts have ruled out Ward (knee) for Thursday night's game against the Texans.
long_comment: Ward's availability for Thursday night's duel against the Texans was in doubt after the veteran corner left Week 10 early with a knee injury. On a short week, the Colts are without the starting cornerback. With Sauce Gardner (calf) also questionable, the secondary could be short come Thursday. Kenneth Harris could see more reps with Ward out.

short_comment: The Colts ruled out Mallory (hamstring) for Thursday night's games against the Texans.
long_comment: Mallory was absent from practice all week heading into Thursday night's divisional showdown versus Houston. This marks the 27-year-old's third straight missed game. He has caught two of nine targets for 20 yards in three games during the 2026 season.

short_comment: Gould (toe) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Texans, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
long_comment: Gould was deemed limited on Monday and Tuesday's practice reports, but he upgraded to a full listing on Wednesday's practice estimate. That suggests that the WR has a solid chance of being available Thursday, but those in leagues deep enough to consider Gould in PPR formats will need to check his availability ahead of the Colts' 8:15 pm ET kickoff. Gould was listed as a starter for this past Sunday's win over the Dolphins alongside Laquon Treadwell and Deion Burks, a contest in which he logged 32 of a possible 59 snaps on offense while catching two of his four targets for 28 yards.

short_comment: out
long_comment: out

short_comment: Walley registered five tackles, a sack, a forced fumble and two pass breakups in Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins.
long_comment: The second-year defensive back was responsible for perhaps the biggest play of the game, as his strip sack of the Dolphins' Kyle McCord early in the third quarter led to a fumble recovery in the end zone by teammate Adetomiwa Adebawore. Walley was named the AFC Defensive Player of the Week for his big performance.

short_comment: Allen posted nine tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: Allen led the Colts in tackles Sunday, and he got to Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss late in the fourth quarter. Allen also picked off McCord earlier in the fourth, although the play was nullified by an illegal contact penalty by Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris. Allen has logged at least 10 tackles in each of his last three outings, and he has accumulated 34 tackles (12 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across seven regular-season games.

short_comment: Dulin caught one of two targets for 30 yards and returned three kickoffs for 77 yards during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles on special teams.
long_comment: Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being sent out at the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Dulin's 13 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Colts wide receivers behind Laquon Treadwell (52), Deion Burks (34) and Anthony Gould (32). Dulin did connect on a 30-yard pass from Daniel Jones late in the second quarter, which was a pivotal part of a nine-play, 92-yard drive that ended with a seven-yard touchdown catch by Treadwell. Dulin has logged catches of 55 and 30 yards in each of his last two outings, and he could be the Colts' WR3 for Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Texans if Gould is not cleared to play due to a toe injury.

short_comment: Burks failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded one tackle on special teams.
long_comment: With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being shipped off at the Nov. 10 deadline, the Colts turned to Burks, Laquon Treadwell and Anthony Gould to serve as the top wideouts for Week 10. Burks' 34 offensive snaps were a season high and second among the team's wide receivers, but the rookie seventh-rounder failed to record a catch for the fifth time in 10 games, with one of his intended passes from Daniel Jones being intercepted midway through the second quarter. Gould is working through a toe injury, so Burks could step into a bigger role on offense against the Texans on Thursday.

short_comment: Indianapolis placed Carlies (neck) on injured reserve Tuesday.
long_comment: Carlies hurt his neck in Week 9 against Dallas and didn't practice at all last week before being ruled out for Sunday's win over the Dolphins. Now that he's landed on IR, the third-year linebacker will need to miss at least the Colts' next four games. Austin Ajiake and West Weeks will likely soak up the rotational defensive snaps that Carlies had been getting.

short_comment: The Colts signed Watkins from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Tuesday.
long_comment: A spot on the 53-man roster opened up when Indianapolis placed linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) on IR, and the team elected to give Watkins the opening. The veteran wideout was elevated for Sunday's Week 10 win over Miami, but he didn't end up playing. With that said, there could be an opportunity for Watkins to garner some work in the passing game after Indianapolis traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs and Keenan Allen to the 49ers last week. Watkins last logged regular-season NFL action in 2023, when he caught 15 of 21 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over nine games with the Eagles.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Shrader made his sole field-goal attempt and converted all three PATs in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: Shrader sole field-goal attempt was a 51-yard make in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker moves to 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-20 on PATs through 10 games of the 2026 regular season.

short_comment: Treadwell caught three passes on as many targets for 24 yards and a touchdown during Indianapolis' 24-22 win over Miami on Sunday.
long_comment: Week 10 was the Colts' first game without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, who were traded to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Tuesday. Treadwell led all Colts wide receivers with three catches and 52 offensive snaps, and he connected with Daniel Jones for a seven-yard touchdown pass late in the second quarter to give Indianapolis a 14-7 halftime lead. It was the first time Treadwell found the end zone this season, and the 2016 first-rounder figures to maintain a larger role in the offense given the departure of the Colts' top targets at the trade deadline. The Colts will hit the road for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday, and Houston's defense ranks 28th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing wide receivers.

short_comment: Giddens played two offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick of the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

short_comment: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

short_comment: Jones completed 11 of 22 passes for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while adding five carries for nine yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
long_comment: Jones failed to eclipse the 200-yard mark for the fourth straight game while throwing multiple picks for the second time in that span. Neither turnover led to any Dolphins points, and Jones also threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to new interim No. 1 receiver Laquon Treadwell in the second quarter. Jones has completed just 59.6 percent of his passes and has a 7:12 TD:INT across 10 games, and with Indianapolis devoid of any realistic postseason aspirations, it may not be long before Anthony Richardson is given an opportunity under center. However, Joel A. Erickson of The Indy Star reports that head coach Shane Steichen has already named Jones the starter for Thursday's Week 11 road matchup against the Texans.

short_comment: Warren rushed once for three yards and brought in two of three targets for one yard in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
long_comment: The new-look Colts offense was without Josh Downs and Keenan Allen after trade-deadline moves, but Warren was still surprisingly uninvolved. Daniel Jones completed only 50.0 percent of his passes and threw for just 108 yards, however, so Warren's minimal production is somewhat understandable in that context. Jones has thrown for under 200 yards in four consecutive games and is playing generally uninspired football, so Warren's fantasy outlook remains shaky for the time being but could improve if Anthony Richardson takes over under center at some point.

short_comment: Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis.
long_comment: Taylor made it through the trade deadline unscathed after rumors swirled around a possible change of scenery, but the talented back still split plenty of work with rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan, who logged 12 carries. Taylor still remained the No. 1 option and was the only one of the two to see any targets, and the rushing yardage total was his best since Week 7, just before serious trade speculation began. Taylor is staying put for the rest of the campaign, but it seems likely that he'll continue ceding a fair share of touches to McGowan moving forward.

short_comment: The Colts placed Davis-Gaither (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
long_comment: Davis-Gaither was already ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami in what would be his second consecutive missed contest due to a knee injury. Now that he's been placed on IR, the seventh-year pro will be required to miss at least four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Titans on Sunday, Dec. 20.

short_comment: Key (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
long_comment: Key missed the Colts' last five games while on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 4 against the Commanders. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions, which gave the Colts the confidence to activate the veteran defensive lineman from IR ahead of Sunday's contest. Prior to his IR stint, Key posted eight tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one forced fumble in four regular-season games.

short_comment: Allen (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Allen is one of three Jaguars running backs on the Week 11 injury report, with Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez (hand) also tending to health concerns. After being listed as a non-participant Thursday, Tuten appears to be more at risk of sitting out Sunday against the Giants than either Allen or Rodriguez, both of whom have been limited in the Jaguars' first two Week 11 practices.

short_comment: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Tuten was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, so his downgrade in activity a day later is notable, though the listing could be maintenance-related rather than due to a setback.  O'Halloran previously relayed that the running back was working off to the side during the media-access portion of Thursday's session. The extent of Tuten's participation in Friday's practice bears watching, as the Jaguars look to determine whether he'll take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.

short_comment: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

short_comment: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

short_comment: Striggow (concussion) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
long_comment: Striggow was forced to check out of Sunday's game at Tennessee after suffering a blow to the head, and he's now dealing with a concussion as the Jaguars begin their Week 11 preparations. If he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, it could signal he's close to clearing concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

short_comment: Johnson (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville reports.
long_comment: Johnson returns to limited practice participation after completing Week 10 without any injury designation. The safety overcame an ankle injury to suit up for the Jaguars' Week 9 win over the Ravens but appears to have aggrevated the recovering area in the team's Week 10 win over the Titans. Johnson will need to continue to log limited or full practices during the remaining two Week 11 prep sessions for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

short_comment: Walker (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville reports.
long_comment: Walker injured his ribs in Week 8 against the Colts, but the fifth-year pro was cleared to play in each of the Jaguars' last two games. Unless his practice participation decreases over the next two days, Walker should be good to go for Sunday's road game against the Giants. The 2022 first-rounder has 22 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

long_comment: questionable
