long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen announced Wednesday that Hainsey (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
long_comment: Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.

short_comment: Oluokun finished Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (nine solo).
long_comment: Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.

short_comment: Little went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs during Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: Little was able to make four field-goal tries for the second straight week, converting attempts from 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards in the contest. The kicker has now gone 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.
long_comment: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
long_comment: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

short_comment: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

short_comment: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

short_comment: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.
long_comment: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

short_comment: Strange caught two of three targets for nine yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
long_comment: The Jaguars keep blowing out their opponents, and Strange contributed a three-yard touchdown Sunday but was otherwise not heard from much, as Parker Washington dog-walked the Titans' secondary for 7-152-1 receiving on nine targets. Strange's touchdown grab was his first since Week 1. He remans a locked-in TE1 for fantasy, as he is playing virtually every snap in an elite offense.

short_comment: Green (forearm) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

short_comment: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday.
long_comment: Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

short_comment: The Chiefs activated Norman-Lott (knee) from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
long_comment: Norman-Lott was removed from the PUP list prior to the expiration of his 21-day practice window. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and his participation over the next two days will determine whether he'll make his 2026 regular-season debut against the Cardinals on Sunday. Norman-Lott is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025.

short_comment: Woods (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Woods has missed the Chiefs' last two contests with a neck injury he sustained in the team's Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder now starts Week 11 prep as a full participant, meaning he will likely suit up for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals as a rotational option for the Chiefs' defensive line.

short_comment: Smith (concussion) did not practice Wednesday, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
long_comment: Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons. Even if he practices over the coming days, he would need to clear protocol in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Mike Caliendo would likely start at right guard if Smith doesn't play.

short_comment: Moore (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
long_comment: Moore did not play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Jets in Week 9. He'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity, but if he cannot play against the Cardinals on Sunday, then Joshua Ezeudu would likely start at right tackle for a second consecutive game.

short_comment: The Chiefs placed Wiley (ankle) on injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
long_comment: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

short_comment: Bolton (shin) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Bolton likely picked up the injury during the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons in Week 10, when he posted nine tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble. The sixth-year linebacker will have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

short_comment: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

short_comment: Kelce was a full participant in Wednesday's practice despite being listed with ankle and calf injuries.
long_comment: During this past Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons, Kelce exited for a brief spell in the first half after injuring his ankle, but he ultimately returned to the contest. In addition to the ankle issue, Kelce may have tweaked his calf at some point in Week 10, but head coach Andy Reid indicated prior to Wednesday's practice that the veteran tight end is "doing well" in his recovery from the injuries, per Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com. His ability to take every rep for the Chiefs' first Week 11 session suggests his status for Sunday's game againt the Cardinals isn't in any peril.

short_comment: Tranquill recorded nine total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Falcons.
long_comment: Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

short_comment: Williams recorded five total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Williams was able to register at least five takedowns for the third time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he intercepted a deep pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix. The interception was his second of the year, and he has now compiled 41 total tackles (23 solo) and 11 passes defensed over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

short_comment: Briningstool caught one of two targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 35-13 win against the Jets on Sunday.
long_comment: Briningstool connected with Patrick Mahomes for a 20-yard reception midway through the first quarter but didn't record another reception. The 23-year-old tight end has exactly one catch in each of his past three games. That's not enough production to warrant fantasy consideration, but Briningstool is at least showing growth as a pass catcher, as he had just one catch on two targets over his first six contests of the campaign.

short_comment: Butker made all five PATs in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Butker did not attempt a field goal in the contest, as the Chiefs solely scored touchdowns. He now moves to 27-for-28 on PATs in 2026 as he continues to struggle to hold onto the starting kicker job.

short_comment: Gray caught one of three targets for six yards during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Gray was unable to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after he had at least two catches in each of the team's previous five games prior to Week 9. The tight end did play a season-high 53 offensive snaps with Travis Kelce being limited to just 18 snaps on offense as a result of an ankle injury. If Kelce is forced to be limited or even miss the team's Week 11 matchup with Arizona, Gray would stand to operate as the team's primary tight end in his place.

short_comment: Armstrong caught his only target for a 43-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The wideout played just 17 of 64 offensive snaps against Atlanta and ran only seven pass routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks. Armstrong was tasked with blocking duties on 10 of his snaps. He still managed to catch his first career touchdown in the fourth quarter with the game already well out of hand. Armstrong is not on the fantasy radar.

short_comment: Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

short_comment: Worthy failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons.
long_comment: Worthy ran a team-high 37 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 38 dropbacks, but on a day Mahomes targeted nine different players, Worthy was the only one to not record a catch. With Josh Downs now in the fold and working to get comfortable in the offense, Worthy's role will likely only continue to shrink. On just eight routes in his team debut Sunday, Downs posted a 4-53-1 receiving line on five targets. Worthy hasn't produced that many fantasy points in a game all season. He's waiver-wire fodder in 12-team redraft leagues.

short_comment: Downs secured four of five targets for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled once but recovered and returned three punts for 10 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Making his Chiefs debut following three days of practice after arriving via trade from the Colts on Tuesday, Downs looked right at home in the Patrick Mahomes-led offense. The young wideout fully capitalized on the upgrade he saw at quarterback, finishing third in receptions, receiving yards and targets right out of the gate and adding his second touchdown of the season on a difficult 18-yard catch just before halftime. Downs' immediate chemistry with Mahomes is highly welcome news for fantasy managers, and he'll aim to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

short_comment: Rice brought in five of six targets for 82 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Rice led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in receptions and targets on a prolific afternoon for the Chiefs' air attack. Rice didn't get in on the scoring fun of a five-touchdown day for Patrick Mahomes, but he still eclipsed 80 receiving yards for the third time this season and first time since Week 3. Rice's level of involvement was encouraging given the debuting Josh Downs drew five targets, keeping the former's prospects bright for a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Mahomes completed 22 of 35 passes for 348 yards with five touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 15 yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
long_comment: Taking advantage of a controlled environment and a fast track at Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- not to mention the presence of the debuting Josh Downs -- Mahomes repeatedly exploited the vulnerabilities of the Falcons defense throughout the afternoon. The legendary signal-caller showed no ill effects from the elbow injury that he'd suffered in Week 9, and he connected with Emmett Johnson (12, six yards), Downs (18 yards), Cyrus Allen (39 yards) and Andrew Armstrong (43 yards) for his quintet of touchdown passes. Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. Mahomes will take 2,385 passing yards and a 19:4 TD:INT into a Week 11 home matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

short_comment: Delane (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
long_comment: Delane has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The rookie first-rounder will likely return to his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Nohl Williams, while Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace provide depth at the position.

short_comment: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end didn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers has already cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

short_comment: Booker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

short_comment: Hemingway (upper body) didn't participate in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Hemingway is currently dealing with a stinger, making his status for Sunday's matchup versus Denver uncertain. With Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) also dealing with an injury, the Raiders could find themselves shorthanded along the defensive line against the Broncos, as Thomas Booker is the only healthy defensive end currently on the active roster.

short_comment: Fatukasi (toe) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Fatukasi logged 31 defensive snaps in Week 10 versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have hurt his toe along the way. He'll probably need to practice in full Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

short_comment: Paye (neck) was not listed on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

short_comment: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

short_comment: Gay (hip) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Gay made both of his two field-goal tries and his only extra-point attempt during Sunday's 21-13 loss versus the Seahawks, but it looks like he might have picked up a hip injury at some point along the way. As long as he can manage a full practice Thursday or Friday, he should still be in a good position to suit up in Week 11 against the Broncos.

short_comment: Chinn tallied seven tackles (three solo) in a loss to Seattle on Sunday.
long_comment: Chinn continues to put up consistent tackling numbers, as he's now logged at least seven stops in six straight games. The veteran safety has played all but one of Las Vegas' defensive snaps this season. He's up to 72 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles through 10 contests.

short_comment: Walker posted eight tackles (four solo) and recovered a fumble against Seattle in Sunday's Week 10 loss.
long_comment: Walker, Nakobe Dean and Maxx Crosby all had eight tackles Sunday to co-lead the team. Walker added a fumble recovery on the second play of the game that helped set up a Raiders touchdown. The veteran linebacker has remained productive in his first season with Las Vegas following four years in Green Bay. Walker has 80 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, and two recovered fumbles though 10 contests on the campaign.

short_comment: Dean registered eight tackles (five solo) and recovered a fumble Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Dean tied for the team lead in stops with Maxx Crosby and Quay Walker. Nonetheless, the veteran linebacker saw his five-game streak of double-digit tackles come to an end. Dean did contribute his first recovered fumble of the season when he scooped up a ball that was turned over by Seattle QB Drew Lock in the fourth quarter. Dean is tied with Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton for the NFL lead with 107 tackles, though Denver has played one fewer game.

short_comment: Crosby finished Sunday's loss to Seattle with eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks.
long_comment: Crosby tied for the team lead with his season-high eight stops. Among those tackles, four went for a loss, including a fourth-quarter sack of Drew Lock. After registering just a half-sack over six games from Week 2 to Week 7, Crosby has since finished with exactly 1.0 sacks in each of his past three contests. He's at 5.0 sacks overall through 10 games as he seeks a fifth NFL campaign with double-digit sacks.

short_comment: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
long_comment: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

short_comment: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
long_comment: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

short_comment: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

short_comment: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
long_comment: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

short_comment: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

short_comment: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

short_comment: Mendoza completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 22 yards and one TD during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: The Mendoza era in Las Vegas officially kicked off this week following the trade of veteran QB Kirk Cousins to the Vikings, and the rookie first overall pick unsurprisingly flashed at times while also stalling numerous drives by taking six sacks overall. On a positive note, Mendoza didn't turn the ball over, and he also recorded his first touchdown as a pro on a 10-yard run on the Raiders' opening offensive possession. He'll seek to build on the initial start of his career next Sunday at Denver.

short_comment: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
long_comment: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

short_comment: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
long_comment: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

short_comment: Benson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
long_comment: Benson is a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week. The rookie sixth-rounder has failed to find a place in a wide-open receiving corps so far, and it remains to be seen how coach Klint Kubiak will utilize him.

short_comment: Zuhn (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Zuhn started Week 10 prep with a pair of limited practices before upgrading to full participation in Friday's session. The starting left guard has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the defending champion Seahawks.

short_comment: Kolar (concussion) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice.
long_comment: The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

short_comment: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
long_comment: McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, was also limited Wednesday. Per  Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

short_comment: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

short_comment: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

short_comment: Henley (knee) didn't participate in the Chargers' practice Wednesday.
long_comment: Henley popped up on the injury report Wednesday after compiling 11 tackles (five solo) during the Week 10 win over the Ravens. Marlowe Wax would be in line to start at inside linebacker during Sunday's matchup versus the Jets if Henley ends up being unable to play.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
long_comment: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

short_comment: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
long_comment: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
long_comment: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
long_comment: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
long_comment: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
long_comment: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

short_comment: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
long_comment: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
long_comment: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered.
long_comment: On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. The performance also marked the first time Hampton eclipsed the century mark this season, and he added his fourth rushing touchdown of 2026 on a one-yard power run on fourth down on the first play following the two-minute warning in the first half. Hampton now is up to 474 rushing yards and a 12-63-0 receiving line heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

short_comment: Shelley (ankle) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Shelley is dealing with an apparent ankle injury, and his status for the remainder of the second half is now uncertain. In his absence, Deane Leonard is a top candidate to see an increase in workload in the secondary with Los Angeles.

short_comment: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash after being listed as doubtful following a third consecutive DNP on Saturday, and it's no surprise the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

short_comment: Awosika (fibula) is active for Monday's game against the Ravens.
long_comment: Awosika will suit up Monday for the first time since Week 2, when he suffered an injury to his fibula. He should slide back into his starting role at left guard.

short_comment: Eboigbe (ankle) is inactive for Monday's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
long_comment: Eboigbe suffered an ankle injury against the Texans in Week 9, and he will be sidelined for Monday night's contest. Nick Barrett should see an uptick in defensive snaps in the absence of Eboigbe, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Jets on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Pipkins (knee) won't be available for Monday's game against the Ravens after the Chargers didn't activate him from injured reserve.
long_comment: Pipkins has been sidelined since Week 1, but he had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday and was listed as questionable heading into Monday. Assuming he can continue practicing in Week 11 without issue, Pipkins could be activated ahead of the Chargers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Jets. Once reinstated, Pipkins could settle back in as the team's starting left guard.

short_comment: Taylor (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Monday.
long_comment: Taylor is battling an ankle injury and was ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with Baltimore. Now on injured reserve, he will be required to miss at least four games before being eligible to return.

short_comment: The Chargers activated Perryman (pectoral) from the reserve/injured list ahead of Monday's game versus Baltimore.
long_comment: Perryman is finally cleared to suit up after missing the entire season due to a pec issue. While his return is good news for the Chargers, it may take him a game or two to get back to full speed.

short_comment: Nacua has been suspended three games for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports
long_comment: Nacua currently resides on injured reserve due to PCL and MCL sprains and a turf toe injury, for which he still must miss at least three games. The announced suspension conveniently lines up with his remaining expected time away from the field, and he'll be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14, following the completion of the the Rams' Week 13 contest versus the 49ers. Schefter's report also notes that the league communicated to the wideout that that any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, would subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league.

short_comment: Garrett played 17 defensive snaps but did not show up on the box score otherwise during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
long_comment: Garrett was cleared to play in Week 10 after working through a knee injury. The low snap count was more due to the fact that the Cardinals posted only 35 offensive snaps while recording a 17:37 time of possession. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, so Garrett's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

short_comment: Lake posted two tackles (one solo) during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
long_comment: Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 65 tackles (38 solo), 11 pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through 10 regular-season games heading into the Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

long_comment: out

long_comment: out

short_comment: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

short_comment: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

short_comment: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

short_comment: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

short_comment: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

short_comment: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

short_comment: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
long_comment: The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

short_comment: The Rams placed McMahon (knee) on injured reserve Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
long_comment: McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

short_comment: Smith caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
long_comment: With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

short_comment: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

short_comment: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

short_comment: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
long_comment: Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

short_comment: McDuffie (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
long_comment: McDuffie missed three of the Rams' last four games due to a persistent back injury. The cornerback is all set to suit up for Sunday's game, as he and Kam Curl return to reinforce the Rams' secondary in time for a divisional matchup with the Cardinals' rookie quarterback Carson Beck.

short_comment: Bell (knee) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: After being sidelined first time this season during this past Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, Bell told Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post that his absence was a result of hyperextending his knee in a recent practice. The rookie wideout appears to be healthier in Week 11, however, as he was able to practice in a limited fashion for a second straight day. Bell expects be available for Sunday's game against the Bills, per Furones.

short_comment: Douglas (shoulder) remained a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: The listing makes sense, given that Douglas, who was also deemed limited Wednesday, worked in a  non-contact jersey Thursday. Fellow WR Chris Bell (knee) has also logged back-to-back 'LP' listings, with the duo's game statuses for Sunday's game against the Bills set to be revealed after Friday's practice session.

short_comment: Meyer (neck) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Meyer was forced out of Sunday's game at Indianapolis early with an injury, and now his status for Week 11 is uncertain. With regular starting center Aaron Brewer still in concussion protocol as of Wednesday, 2024 sixth-rounder Jarrett Kingston is currently the Dolphins' top option among centers without any health issues.

short_comment: Baker (knee) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Baker managed to practice in full for a second straight session Wednesday, suggesting he's trending in the right direction as the Dolphins begin their Week 11 preparations. For now, he's still on the reserve/PUP list as Sunday's matchup against the Bills approaches.

short_comment: Brewer (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
long_comment: Brewer sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis due to a concussion, and now his availability for Week 11 is in jeopardy. He'll need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol, which includes getting clearance from an independent neurologist, before he'll be able to return to game action. Whether he's able to practice Thursday or Friday could provide some indication as to any progress he makes ahead of Sunday's game at Buffalo.

short_comment: Wayne (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Wayne sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis with a quad injury, and his availability for Week 11 is now in question. If he's not able to get back onto the practice field Thursday or Friday, he'll be trending toward missing Sunday's game at Buffalo.

short_comment: Brents (neck) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Brents played 42 defensive snaps during Sunday's game at Indianapolis, and it looks like he might have come away from that contest with a neck injury. He'll likely have to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

short_comment: Trader (shoulder/groin) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Trader may have picked up the injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, when he played every defensive snap and finished with six tackles (four solo). The second-year defensive back will have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Bills.

short_comment: Phillips underwent surgery on his injured bicep Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

short_comment: Brooks produced nine total tackles (six solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Brooks was able to register at least nine takedowns for the fourth straight game and seventh time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to strip Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter, but offensive lineman Dalton Tucker was able to jump on the loose ball. Brooks is now up to 84 total tackles (38 solo) while also adding two passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

short_comment: Rodriguez recorded one solo tackle during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

short_comment: Taaffe recorded six total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

short_comment: Johnson recorded four total tackles (three solo) and a pick-six in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
long_comment: Johnson was able to secure an interception for the second straight week, jumping in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the third quarter, ultimately returning the interception for a 59-yard touchdown. The cornerback has now registered 46 total tackles (24 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine games this season.

short_comment: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
long_comment: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

short_comment: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.
long_comment: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

short_comment: Biggers (knee) was placed on injured reserve by the Dolphins on Tuesday.
long_comment: Biggers suffered a lateral meniscus tear in Week 10, and he will now miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while on IR. Fellow defensive lineman Jordan Phillips (biceps) was also placed on IR on Tuesday, and as a result, Kenneth Grant will operate as the team's top dog at defensive tackle moving forward this season.

short_comment: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

short_comment: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
long_comment: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

short_comment: Head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Willis (groin/core) has not undergone surgery and that the Dolphins are still determining if a procedure is needed, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
long_comment: Per Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald, Hafley noted on that subject Monday, "We will see how he feels. If he needs surgery, he will have surgery," while adding that if the QB does undergo a procedure, it wouldn't "necessarily" be season ending. In any case, the earliest Willis can come off IR is Week 14, with Kyle McCord and Brady Cook currently available to handle Miami's signal-caller duties.

short_comment: Hockenson (wrist) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
long_comment: After sitting out this past Sunday's win at Green Bay due to wrist and chest injuries, Hockenson has logged back-to-back capped sessions to begin Week 11 prep due to just the wrist issue. He'll have one more opportunity to get back to full Friday, at which point the Vikings may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

short_comment: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.
long_comment: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

short_comment: The Vikings placed Richter (foot) on injured reserve Wednesday.
long_comment: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

short_comment: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Van Ginkel sustained a quadriceps injury during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10. His ability to practice Wednesday indicates that the injury isn't a serious one, and an increase in participation over the coming days would put Van Ginkel on track to play in Sunday's road game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

short_comment: Cashman (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
long_comment: Cashman was unable to play against the Packers in Week 10 due to a concussion, although head coach Kevin O'Connell expressed optimism Wednesday that Cashman should clear the league's protocol and return for Sunday's road contest against the 49ers, per Alec Lewis of The Athletic. Cashman would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be cleared to play.

short_comment: The Vikings signed Jones (shoulder) off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
long_comment: Jones was elevated from the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster for both Week 5 and Week 10 against the Saints and Packers, respectively, and he'll now be part of Minnesota's 53-man roster moving forward. He picked up a shoulder injury during Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay and was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, so his reps over the coming days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the 49ers on Nov. 22. The addition of Jones to the active roster gives the Vikings extra depth at wide receiver in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb).

short_comment: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
long_comment: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

short_comment: questionable
long_comment: questionable

short_comment: Murray (hamstring) will miss Wednesday's practice, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
long_comment: The Vikings are targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 29, for Murray to be available again, so his lack of activity this week doesn't come as a susprise. Whenever Murray is back, though, he likely will take on No. 2 QB duties due to the arrival of Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas at the trade deadline.

short_comment: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Addison underwent thumb surgery earlier this week and won't be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
long_comment: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

short_comment: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.
long_comment: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

short_comment: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

short_comment: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
long_comment: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

short_comment: Bartholomew caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: With T.J. Hockenson (wrist) inactive, Bartholomew played 53 of 69 offensive snaps against Green Bay and caught the second of Kirk Cousins' two touchdowns, scoring from 20 yards out in the fourth quarter to give Minnesota a comfortable 27-10 lead. While Ben Yurosek got the start, Bartholomew played 13 more snaps and out-targeted Yurosek four to one. Cousins has an affinity for throwing to his tight ends, so Bartholomew will be on the fantasy radar if Hockenson needs to miss more time.

short_comment: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

short_comment: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
long_comment: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

short_comment: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
long_comment: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

short_comment: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
long_comment: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

short_comment: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
long_comment: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

short_comment: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
long_comment: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

short_comment: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
long_comment: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

short_comment: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
long_comment: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
long_comment: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

short_comment: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
long_comment: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.
